what: The call returns: after a finished part, a later canvas, damage, a loss, a failed attempt or a move, the room calls for hands again.
change: A loop on P01 (the call): arrows into P01 from P11 (a work marked as up), P13 (carrying on), P05 (keeping, under damage) and P10 (the move after a loss), or a clause in P01's statement that the call recurs at those points. The model now has the call only at the start (A02, A01) and the account grounds no loop.
why: Three room forms specify P01 by link lines at 1.4 to 1.7 times the 558 defining rooms' share: C, The design reopened (14 defining rooms), D, Keeping, with help or carrying on (16), and F, Moving for the spot (6); read whole, 23 of these rooms' lines say the call came again at one of those points (C 7, D 11, F 5).
note: A proposal, not an amendment: it can enter a later model only through a supported return to the affected rooms' original leads and a new validation cycle.

what: The answer that asks for a task: a member who answers a call can join and ask where, how or what to place, or give a reason; the bare one-line join is one form of acceptance among others.
change: P15's range would include a willing answer that asks for a task, and A12's mechanism would read the bare join as the most common written acceptance, not the only one. F-023's count (25 of 31 read acceptances bare) stands.
why: Form F, Moving for the spot, restricts A12 in 10 of 34 defining rooms (29 per cent, against 23 of the 558); its lines say answers asked where or how to help, or gave reasons. Branch F35 (the call made workable) states the same exchange from both ends: A12 restricted in 8 of its 18 members (notes-D5.md, D5a-35).

what: A proposal that is itself the call: a member's start and the room's first call for hands can be one post or one turn.
change: A02's bound, which covers a call before the proposal, would also say that the start and the first call can coincide, so the order A02 states is not observable there; the arrow itself is unchanged.
why: Forms D, Keeping, with help or carrying on, and E, The sub's play, run as work, restrict A02 in 12 and 11 defining rooms; by the D5 restrict sorts, 12 of D's 12 lines and 8 of E's 11 say the start and the call share one post or turn (the sort's class neither: they coincide). Branch F32 found the same in 7 of its 8 restricting members (notes-D5.md, D5a-32).

what: After the move, the room builds again: a new spot or a replacement plan is followed by a new start and reports of the new work.
change: An arrow from P10 (the move after a loss) to P03 (building and reporting the mark's state). With PR-D6-01 (the call returns) it would give the loss, move and building sequence the account calls ungrounded its return.
why: Form F, Moving for the spot, specifies P03 by link lines in 12 of 34 defining rooms (35 per cent, against 23 of the 558); F09's rooms in F hold 8 of them. Branch F09 (the move returns to building) stands on 55 re-check lines in 54 rooms, with no within-case dating, so the order has not been tested against a null (notes-D5.md, D5a-09).

what: The room sizes its design to its hands, its space and its colours before any loss.
change: A link from K02 (the room judges it has too few hands or too little room) to P02 (the room settles what its mark shows). The model gives K02 one consequence, A10 (the move after a loss); this would add a second, before any loss.
why: Branch F34 (the design sized to the hands) found the judgement coming first and sizing the design in 10 of its 22 members (notes-D5.md, D5a-34). At the form level, F34's rooms hold the P02 lines that specify the design in form C, The design reopened (4 rooms), and in form E, The sub's play, run as work (5 rooms).

what: The check before repair: before undoing pixels that differ from the form they know, keepers refresh the canvas, ask for the intended form or check whether the change is intended.
change: A step inside P05 (keeping): checking the current canvas and the intended form before a repair. It is a route by which keepers learn of a planned change other than being told, beside the two the held P05 proposal names (the change read from its shape; informed members holding it). P05's statement and the held proposal are not changed by this proposal; findings F-024 to F-027 stand as they are.
why: Form D, Keeping, with help or carrying on, specifies P05 by add-step lines in 21 of 96 defining rooms (22 per cent, against 14 of the 558); five of them say keepers checked before repairing, and one room of form A says the same in a link line. Branch F27's note records the step from the room models of r/OnePiece, r/cowchop and r/armok (notes-D5.md, D5a-27).

what: The terms bind the placers they reach: a settled border is kept by the placers who learn its terms and accept them, and by the scripts whose targets are changed; placers the terms do not reach keep placing.
change: A bound on A05 (a settled border is a line members keep): 'This holds for the placers the terms reach, told in the thread or the chat, and for the scripts whose targets are changed.' A05's statement, P21, A21 and F-020 are not changed by this proposal. It states for A05 the border half of F-026, the telling clause at the border.
why: Three forms change A05. Form A restricts it in 39 of 135 defining rooms (28.9 per cent, against 21.5 per cent of the 558); form B adds conditions in 16 of 113 (14.2 against 10.2); form D adds conditions in 13 of 96 (13.5 against 10.2). In 24 of these rooms (A 8, B 12, D 4) the line says restraint followed where placers learned and accepted the terms; in 8 of the 24 the terms had to reach a script's target. Branch F26 explains A's cell and branch F08 B's (fractal-D6.jsonl). The other lines say restraint came before any settlement, by the room's own norm, as F-020 states.

what: Help comes from the hands a helper can spare: a room gives help when its own work is finished or safe and it has placements to spare, and holds help back while its own defence is short.
change: A condition added to P16 (help between rooms): help is given from spare hands, once the helper's own work is safe or finished. A bound on A13 (short of hands, a room turns to other rooms): the shortage brings the request; whether help comes depends on the other room's spare hands. P16's and A13's statements are not changed by this proposal.
why: Forms C and D restrict A13: 30 of 96 defining rooms in C (31.2 per cent, against 26.0 of the 558) and 33 of 96 in D (34.4). In 12 of them the line says the help came from the donor's surplus or waited on it (C 5, D 7). Branch F22 explains D's P16 and A13 cells: in 6 more of its rooms in D help waits on the helper's secure work and spare pixels; branch F28 states the same at the border in form A (3 more rooms). In 12 other restrict lines a request under strain is recorded and arriving help is not shown (my reading); the record cannot show whether it came.

what: Border talk before keeping: a room talks with its neighbours when it seeks a spot, and when its building runs into a neighbour's work, before it has a mark to keep.
change: Two arrows into P08 (border terms), beside A04 (keeping the mark brings the room to its neighbours): from P27 (choosing the spot before any loss), where a room asks a neighbour for permission or access before it builds; and from P03 (building), where a neighbour objects to the room's construction or expansion over its work. A04's statement is not changed by this proposal; P27 stays a candidate.
why: Form F, Moving for the spot, restricts A04 in 13 of 34 defining rooms (38.2 per cent, against 22.9 of the 558). In 6 of the 13 the border talk came while the room sought a spot or permission to build; in 6 it came when building or a script crossed a neighbour's work (my reading of the lines). No branch explains the cell: F09's rooms hold 4 of the 13 lines, but F09's change is building again after a move; the reading rests on the form's lines alone.

what: The play run as work: inside the sub's April Fools key, moderators and members do organized work with the steps the model gives the canvas work. They start the play and set its rules, enforce the rules by real removals and bots, test whether claims are jokes, repair what the play breaks, argue and set its end, and ask that its changes last.
change: A process element under Host framing, beside K01: the sub administers its play. K01's statement (the key) is not changed by this proposal. The element would bring into the model what the ruling of D3a-55 put outside its scope, the sub's own business on the canvas days, so it is a change of scope as well as a new element; a later model decides whether the scope is widened.
why: Three forms specify K01 by add-step lines: E in 56 of 84 defining rooms (66.7 per cent, against 103 of the 558, 18.5 per cent), D in 24 of 96 (21 of its 24 holders are rooms of D.2, Keeping inside the sub's play) and F in 9 of 34. Branch F01 (103 rooms) states the change; its rooms are 54 of these holders in E, 23 in D and 9 in F, and its five subforms (F02 to F06) lean to E. In the lines read, the play runs beside the canvas work; in a few rooms it reaches it (r/battlecats and r/bindingofisaac, D5a-02; r/osu and r/polandball, d6a06_D06_hows.txt and F21's line).
